calls.reason: Huang et al. show intrinsic self-correction failing, but SelfCheckGPT shows partial factuality detection. No study independently measures understanding or shows it causes the listed failures.

FActScore documents frequent factual errors, but Kıcıman et al. report strong causal-reasoning benchmark results alongside unpredictable failures. No evidence links hallucinations to an absence of common sense.
The only evidence is OpenAI's general statement about anti-regurgitation measures. Nothing dated shows this specific example was filtered or blocked by February 2024.

The Walters and Wilder study supports the LLM side with high rates of fabricated citations. The human evidence comes from suggestion-induced false-memory studies, not spontaneous invention, so the comparison is unsettled.
Extraction studies show verbatim training text emitted by ChatGPT, and Carlini et al. find larger models memorize more. The data-volume part is less clear given the 2025 Morris et al. findings.
LeCun's November 2023 post agrees that LLM understanding is superficial, but his 2022 Noema essay already said the same. A recent shift isn't shown, and nothing establishes Hinton's awareness.
